management: removal of honeysuckle may require a combination of several methods. 1). for small infestations, hand pulling can be effective. wearing gloves, pull the plants out by the roots. try to get as much of the root system as possible to prevent regrowth. 2). for larger infestations, cutting the honeysuckle down to the ground and then digging out the roots can be effective. use loppers or a saw to cut the plants as close to the ground as possible, and then dig out the roots. 3). herbicides can be effective in killing honeysuckle but be cautious as they can harm other plants as well. glyphosate-based or triclopyr-based herbicides are commonly used for honeysuckle control. 4). girdling involves cutting a ring around the stem of the honeysuckle, which interrupts the flow of nutrients and kills the plant. 5). regularly mowing or trimming the honeysuckle can weaken it over time.

management: to control moss, try the following cultural methods: (1) let the sunshine in; (2) mow properly; (3) manage soil moisture properly; and (4) create good soil conditions for healthy grass. increase sunlight by pruning trees to at least 6 feet from the ground and thinning branches. mow once a week to keep your lawn between 2-3 inches. add lime to maintain the ph around 6.0-6.5. feed your lawn with a product high in nitrogen, low in phosphorus, and moderate in potassium. irrigate properly by installing french drains or a rain garden and watering ¼ inch each time, 4 to 6 times a week. if these methods don’t work, consider raking or dethatching your lawn in mossy areas, overseeding, and applying fertilizer. chemical products can be used as a last resort.
